purpose: Triage whether the three pstack siblings of /correct overlap it, whether item 18 is carried by it, and whether any has an execution, network or self-update surface.
mechanism:
All three are prose-only SKILL.md files with `disable-model-invocation: true` (reflect:4, encode-lessons:4, architect:4).

(1) encode-lessons vs /correct. encode-lessons is a principle. It fires when "you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time" (encode-lessons:3, :14). It gives a four-rung ladder (unrepresentable state, then lint/banned API, then canonical helper, then runtime check; :19). It adds "if structural, only use the structural fix" (:21) and a capture/route/close loop that routes one-offs to a brain note, recurring fixes to a skill or lint, and systemic issues to a principle (:23-26). The trigger is reactive and per-incident, and the only evidence is the agent's own awareness.

/correct (~/.claude/jobs/112d1b58/tmp/cursor-correct-SKILL.md) takes the same ladder and operationalises it as a repo sweep. So yes, it is essentially encode-lessons plus a sweep. Where it goes beyond encode-lessons:
- Mining step: it reads commits, reverts, review comments, agent instruction files and workaround comments (correct:15). encode-lessons has no mining step.
- Class threshold: "A class counts once it has happened twice" (correct:15). encode-lessons only says to decide one-off vs pattern (:24).
- Level 1 is named architecture work: one owner per piece of state, hide internals so the wrong import fails, replace hand-synced lists with one source of truth, delete old ways an agent would copy (correct:19). encode-lessons' top rung is only "unrepresentable state" (:19).
- A test-quality rule: fix or delete any test that still passes if every function it calls returned nothing (correct:21).
- Lint ergonomics: the error must name the file, type or function to use instead, and where a pattern is already common, fail only when a change adds more (correct:20). That is a ratchet.
- Proof gate: "Prove each new check fails on a real past mistake" (correct:26). encode-lessons has no proof requirement.
- Same command locally and in CI, and exceptions carried on the line with a reason, an expiry date and a human's approval (correct:26).
- A rule table pairing each rule with its enforcer. A rule that exists but is unenforced when the operator corrects again counts as a repeat and must be fixed at the highest level in the same change. Rules are dropped once the mistake is impossible (correct:30). This is a recurring-failure escalation and a prune rule, and encode-lessons has neither.
- Reply contract: each class with its evidence, the level picked, and why no higher level worked (correct:32).
- Agent-as-contributor design stance (correct:11).
What encode-lessons has that /correct lacks: the brain-note routing for one-offs, and the anti-patterns list (:28-31). /correct's own "A class counts once it has happened twice" implicitly drops one-offs.

(2) Item 18. The 2026-09-18 vet row 18 reads "Missed-trigger transcript check and structural-enforcement demotion gate", sourced from reflect's divergent-reviewer and synthesizer step 4, with proposed home memory-dream or memory-mine, effort M (docs/vets/2026-09-18-pstack-harness-vet.md:161). It was PARKED in the 2026-09-20 dispositions (:272). Its trigger is recorded on #1202, not in the file, so the "planted-defect fixture" wording comes from the digest and I could not verify it here.

The demotion-gate half is reflect step 4: for any Accepted item "that would be enforced more reliably by a lint rule, script, metadata flag, or runtime check, move it from Accepted to Backlog", citing encode-lessons (reflect:47-49). /correct carries the same idea in a different place. It applies the ladder to repo mistakes, with "docs last, only for judgment calls" (correct:22) and "why a higher level didn't work" (correct:32). It does not gate a reflect-style Accepted list of skill edits.

The missed-trigger half (did a skill that should have fired not fire; reflect:61 "tune description" routing) has no counterpart in /correct. So the 2026-10-07 fixture would exercise only the demotion half, and only on code-repo mistakes. Row 18's home was memory tooling, where context-file rules are the target, and rent-check E2 already provides a promotion ladder there (digest line 16).

(3) architect. Its relevant content is Phase B: assume "the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo" (architect:37). That sentence is near-verbatim identical to correct:11. Beyond it, it screens candidates against references/design-red-flags.md (architect:37), which is not in my input. It also prefers interface depth (:39). Phases E and its tells (:63-70) cover scrapping a wrong architecture. These all act at design time, before the code exists, and are fed by arena runners. /correct's level 1 acts retroactively on existing repo classes (correct:19). The overlap is the shared design stance and the "one source of truth" and "hide internals" instincts. It is not the mining, the proof gate or the rule table. The red-flags file is the only content that could materially overlap level 1, and I did not read it.

(4) Execution, network and self-update surface. No scripts, hooks or dependencies in any file. Findings:
- reflect:21-22 is a bash `ls -t ... *.jsonl | head -10` over the agent-transcripts directory. It is inline instruction, read-only, and the file explicitly forbids globbing across `~/.cursor/projects/*/` to avoid reading unrelated private chats (:19). It then reads the first JSONL line of each candidate (:27).
- reflect:31 spawns three subagents with `readonly: false` and MCP access, deliberately (readonly strips MCPs). The synthesizer is also non-readonly (:45). That is a wide-permission subagent fan-out, and transcript contents are passed to models named in the `pstack-models.mdc` rule (reflect:33-39). That rule is an external config file that sets which model slugs receive the transcript. Defaults are claude-opus-5-5-xhigh and grok-4.7-xhigh-fast, so the transcript goes to a third-party model by default (reflect:38).
- reflect:53-55 is gated by explicit user approval before applying. Backlog items, however, "file ... automatically" to a tracker (:55). That is an unprompted external write.
- reflect references references/*.md files (judgment, tooling, divergent, synthesizer) that are not in my input.
- architect:31 and :33 call the arena skill with external runners (same model-rule dependency); no URLs appear.
- encode-lessons: none.
- No URL fetch, no curl, no self-update or version-check channel in any of the three. The pstack-models.mdc rule and the arena/how/why/create-skill/interrogate skills are unvendored sibling dependencies.
fit_and_overlap:
encode-lessons: no covering incumbent in the form of a skill. The nearest control surfaces are the global CLAUDE.md root-cause prose, which has no enforcer (digest:18), and rent-check RUBRIC E2, a promotion ladder for context-file rules only (digest:16). encode-lessons is a strict subset of /correct's ladder, so it adds nothing if /correct is adopted. Its brain-note routing maps to the memory feedback type, which is the existing surface (digest:15).

reflect: no direct incumbent for the three-reviewer transcript fan-out. memory-mine, memory-dream and /retro are the adjacent surfaces (digest:5, :15). Item 18 stays parked; see mechanism (2).

architect: no incumbent skill for pre-code design sketching in the digest. The overlap with /correct is only the one shared sentence (architect:37 / correct:11), and the other pstack-specific content depends on arena and how/why skills the harness does not have vendored (not verified). The vet history says pstack components are vendored one at a time with an UPSTREAM.md pin (digest:24).

Net: /correct is the only one of the four that adds a mining step, a proof gate and a rule table. The three siblings do not substitute for it.
maintenance: Not assessed beyond the digest: pstack moved 0.15.7 to 0.15.15 since /correct landed (digest:4). I did not check whether these three files changed in that window. If vendored they would need UPSTREAM.md pins and the vendored-drift-check.sh watch (digest:24).
dependencies: reflect depends on the `pstack-models.mdc` rule, the Task tool with generalPurpose subagents, MCP servers, four references/*.md prompt templates, create-skill, and the encode-lessons skill. architect depends on the how, why, arena, interrogate and principle skills plus references/runner-prompt.md, design-red-flags.md and rationale-template.md. encode-lessons has none. All are Cursor-oriented (the ~/.cursor/projects path at reflect:19 and Task `readonly` semantics), so porting to Claude Code needs path and tool translation (inferred, not tested).
red_flags: reflect:31,45 spawns non-readonly subagents with MCP access over the full transcript, and sends that transcript to model slugs set by an external rule file (default includes grok-4.7-xhigh-fast, reflect:38). That is a data-egress and permission-breadth concern if ported as-is.
reflect:55 auto-files Backlog items to a tracker with no approval, while only the Accepted list is gated (:53-55).
reflect:19 hardcodes Cursor transcript layouts (:25). Not directly portable to Claude Code session JSONL.
The `Why parked` trigger text for item 18 is not in the vet file (only 'recorded on #1202', :272), so the 'planted-defect fixture' condition is taken from the digest, not independently seen.
reflect, architect and the reference files were each not independently validated for behaviour. Only text was read.
unread_files: reflect references/judgment-reviewer.md, tooling-reviewer.md, divergent-reviewer.md, synthesizer.md (not in cand/)
architect references/design-red-flags.md, runner-prompt.md, rationale-template.md (not in cand/)
GitHub issue #1202 (where item 18's trigger is recorded)
/tmp/hv-correct-2026-10-07/cand/correct-PR-494-body.md (not read; verification claims taken from digest)

claims_to_verify.claim: Item 18's trigger on #1202 is exactly 'a planted-defect fixture showing a missed trigger', so a /correct fixture (which tests mistake-class mining and fix level) does not discharge it. It exercises at most the demotion half, not the missed-trigger half.
claims_to_verify.why_verdict_changing: If the #1202 trigger is only about the demotion gate, the 2026-10-07 fixture could discharge item 18. If it is about missed triggers, it must re-park.

claims_to_verify.claim: design-red-flags.md in architect does not contain level-1 architecture fixes (single owner, hide internals, single source of truth, delete dead code) beyond what correct:19 already says.
claims_to_verify.why_verdict_changing: If it contains a full red-flag catalogue for those fixes, architect overlaps /correct's level 1 materially, and could be a cheaper source of level-1 guidance.

claims_to_verify.claim: reflect's references templates contain no network or script execution beyond the Task/MCP use named in SKILL.md.
claims_to_verify.why_verdict_changing: The no-execution-surface finding covers SKILL.md only. Any extraction of reflect text into the harness requires the reference files to be clean.
